title: Contextual Trace Bridge and Burn-Rate Fusion for SLO Root-Cause
creator: Anissa Patel
description: Problem: We have multiple alerting paths (metrics burn-rate, trace-derived error spikes, and log-based anomaly hits) that frequently trigger separate pages for the same underlying incident. Investigators lose time correlating signals across systems. Goal: Build a lightweight 'trace bridge' that attaches rich trace/context metadata to metric and log-derived signals and a burn-rate fusion layer that de-duplicates and scores concurrent alerts for a single paging decision.
background: Recent incidents showed 3x duplicate pages when a downstream KV cache regression increased latency. Dashboards show metric burn-rate firing, logs flagged by anomaly detectors, and traces with high tail latency but no automated correlation. Stakeholders: SRE, Runtime, Platform Observability, Oncall leads. Prior art: ENG-7043 (adaptive burn/paging) and ENG-8291 (trace hooks) implemented pieces; this ticket combines schema, enrichment, scoring, and paging policy integration.
acceptance_criteria: A lightweight trace enrichment pipeline exists that can attach span-level tags (route, model_variant, tenant_id, request_bucket) to metric alerts and log anomalies within 2s of the originating signal.
A fusion service consumes metric burn-rate alerts and log anomaly events, queries traces via the trace bridge, and returns a single scored incident object within 5s for paging decision.
Paging policy updated to prefer fused incidents: duplicate alerts suppressed if score >= 0.75 and root-cause trace exists; otherwise standard burn-rate rules apply.
End-to-end test harness that replays historical incidents and shows reduction in duplicate pages by >=40% on test data set.
Playbook (confluence) and runbook links updated with new triage flow and rollback instructions.
Dashboard tile added to Console showing fusion score distribution, suppression rate, and average correlation latency.
Benchmarks: tracer overhead <2% on 95th percentile request latency when enrichment is enabled in sampling path.
design_notes:
- Approach: build a small service (trace-bridge) that receives lightweight context pointers from the tracing agent (trace_id, span_id, route, model_variant, tenant_id). The bridge stores transient context in a short-lived KV (TTL 2 minutes) keyed by trace_id and offers an indexed lookup API used by the fusion service.
- Fusion: when a metric burn-rate or log-anomaly event arrives, the fusion service queries the bridge with candidate trace_ids (if present), fetches trace context and constructs a similarity score based on route/tenant/model overlap, error signature, and temporal proximity.
- Scoring: heuristic ensemble with weights (route: 0.35, tenant: 0.25, error_signature: 0.25, time_decay: 0.15). Later replaced by a lightweight ML model if needed.
- Sampling: preserve current sampling defaults but inject higher-fidelity context for P0 routes and top-1k tenants.
- Privacy: trace bridge stores only metadata (no raw payloads) and honors tenant-level redaction flags.
implementation_plan: 1) Add minimal span tags in runtime tracer agent (PR: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/3128). 2) Implement trace-bridge service with Redis TTL index and HTTP lookup API (internal repo: observability/trace-bridge). 3) Implement fusion service that subscribes to AlertStream and AnomalyStream; produce a fused incident to Pager pipeline. 4) Update PagerPolicy service to consult fusion results before sending page. 5) Add dashboard widgets and telemetry checks. 6) Run canary for two weeks on staging then 1 week shadow on prod routes. 7) Flip suppression policy behind feature flag. 8) Postmortem & metrics review after 30 days.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Additional latency on alert pipeline causing slower pages. Mitigation: keep lookup and scoring synchronous but bounded (timeout 5s) and fall back to original burn-rate policy on timeout.
Risk: False suppression hides critical incidents. Mitigation: conservative default score threshold (0.75) and mirrored paging for first 72h; extensive replay testing on last 6 months of incidents.
Risk: Increased load on tracing ingest. Mitigation: only add span metadata for top-tier tenants and P0 routes; evaluate adaptive sampling if overhead detected.
Risk: Data retention/privacy. Mitigation: bridge stores metadata only, TTL 2 minutes, logs redaction enforced; security review required for production rollout step.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for bridge API and scoring logic.
- Integration test: synthetic burn-rate + trace injection replay that confirms correct match/no-match outcomes.
- Load test: simulate 10k alerts/min to validate lookup latencies and Redis sizing.
- Chaos test: delay bridge responses to validate fallback behavior.
- Replay test: run fusion logic against last 6 months of alert traces and measure duplicate page rate reduction. Results documented in Confluence link below.
rollout_plan: Stage 1 (staging): enable bridge + fusion in staging for 72h, exercise replay harness. Stage 2 (shadow prod): run fusion in shadow mode for 7 days and evaluate false suppression. Stage 3 (canary): enable suppression for 10% of oncall rotations. Stage 4: global rollout behind feature flag after metrics validation.
